wins.text: Net sales of $2.13B in Q3 2025, up 11.7% YoY — second consecutive quarter above $2B; strongest quarterly daily sales rate since Q1 2023
EPS of $0.29/share, up 12.3% YoY (post 2:1 stock split); net income up 12.6% YoY
Operating margin expanded 40 bps YoY to 20.7%; gross margin up 40 bps to 45.3%, driven by fastener expansion project and supplier initiatives
FMI digital sales grew ~18% YoY, representing 45.3% of total sales (up from 43% a year ago); total installed FMI device base grew 8.7% YoY to ~134,000 devices
Fastener sales grew over 15% in September, outpacing overall company growth; sites spending over $50K/month grew 15.4% YoY; national account sales up double digits

risks.text: Pricing contribution came in at only 240–270 bps in Q3, below the previously stated goal of 3%–5% by end of Q3; Q4 pricing goal revised down to 3.5%–5.5% from prior 5%–8%
Potential gross margin squeeze in Q4 2025 as tariff-driven costs continue to rise and pricing actions lag; management explicitly warned of this risk
Industrial economy remains sluggish with PMI averaging ~48.6 in Q3 (contraction territory); macro demand improvement not expected until 2026
Trade policy and tariff uncertainty creating customer caution and demand pause; limited visibility into Q4 demand; Christmas holiday falling mid-week may cause longer-than-normal shutdowns

Americas business outside the U.S. (particularly Mexico) having a tough year due to heavy OEM/manufacturing skew and sub-50 ISM; SG&A employee costs growing faster than sales due to bonus/commission resets

guidance_items.detail: Full-year 2025 gross profit percentage expected to be relatively flat with 2024, supported by fastener expansion project
Q4 like-for-like pricing impact revised down to 3.5%–5.5% from prior goal of 5%–8%
Full-year 2025 capex expected in range of $235M–$255M, up from $214M in 2024, driven by FMI devices, DC outlays, IT and vehicles
Q4 gross margin expected to decline sequentially (consistent with historical seasonality); potential price/cost squeeze flagged

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Magnitude and mechanics of Q3 bonus/commission reset driving SG&A above expectations
Whether customer inventory pre-buying in H1 pulled forward demand ahead of tariff price increases
Competitive dynamics — whether peers are pushing through less price, signaling increased competition
